items.title: Chico Hamilton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 30, 2000
items.q: Benny Goodman, Benny Goodman’s music. ... But it’s like how many Benny Goodman bands really did it?

ctx.x: My name is Monk Rowe and we’re filming in Manhattan today, and I’m very, very pleased to have Chico Hamilton with me, who has had a long, illustrious and varied career in music. Would you mind telling me what you’re up to in the year 2000?

Sure. I’m just trying to stay alive. No, as a matter of fact we’re up to a whole lot of things. The group, my orchestra — I don’t refer to it as a band, it’s an orchestra, because I think we try to cover all facets of music, not just one direction you know, and not just necessarily under the terminology of even jazz — J-A-Z-Z. I really disapprove of the word myself. I’m in complete accordance with people, with Duke Ellington, Miles Davis, people like that. Why not call it just my music, Chico’s music? Duke…
Right. Does it make a problem, if you’re trying to find a record label to promote your work, they need to put a title to what it is? If you don’t want to call it jazz but they do?

items.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I’d wake up every morning going to school listening to Benny Goodman... they used to let us out of school to go down to the train station and meet the bands... Benny Goodman

ctx.x: Okay, so let’s go back and look at your involvement with music. You say you picked up the clarinet because your buddy Jack was playing it. What kind of music were you listening to and what kind of music were you playing?

There was only one kind of music at that time, which was dynamite, was swing. Man, I’d wake up every morning going to school listening to Benny Goodman, right, (musical sounds) Don’t Be That Way, and Gene Krupa used to (musical sounds). First of all man, that was the beautiful thing about LA, the educational system. The requirement you had to take some form of music, either it was playing an instrument, whatever, music theory or whatever, listening or whatever. You had to be involved with some kind of music…
So what did you do when you went to meet the band? You would stand on the platform when they came off?
